palette.notes: Frames (HM2): hot magenta floors, red brick, teal accents, black/white checker and stripe rugs, white-suited enemies, red blood; score text white with pink/cyan outline. Masks are flat signature colours (red rooster, yellow tiger, teal helmet). Art by Dennis Wedin (wiki). No metrics, no count.

lighting: No modelled light on the sprites: flat fills with dark outlines. Mood comes from saturated floor colours and full-screen tints; the title card is a yellow rooster mask alone on black.
silhouette: Top-down figures are tiny against big rooms and read by colour (white suits vs the hero's mask colour) and by the head/mask shape; corpses stay on the floor as dark-outlined shapes in red pools, so the room keeps a readable record of what happened.

motion.timing: No metrics file. In the frames a room goes from standing enemies to bodies in pools within a couple of seconds; score popups (+400pts, 600PTS) stack and linger over the action. The 'Do you like hurting other people?' card flickers between dim and bright text across ~2 s on a static mask.

texture: Patterned floors carry the texture (checkerboards, stripes, wood planks, tiled kitchens); blood splats and score text layer on top as the real 'texture' of a cleared room.
camera: Top-down and close on the hero's area; the view drifts and leans toward the aim direction (per the wiki), so rooms are cropped and the edge of the screen keeps changing.
sound: Synthwave/electronic soundtrack meant to feel like a film score; combat music switches to ambience once a building is cleared (per the wiki).

acting.enters: Hero walks in from the car at the map edge after an answering-machine intro (per the wiki); fan edits cut to the big mask face popping into a screen corner as the 'enter' beat.
acting.acts: Short decisive bursts, then the bodies stay where they fell while score text pops above them; the mask card is a still face with flickering question text.
acting.exits: Walks back out through the cleared, blood-marked rooms to the car while music drops to ambience (per the wiki).
acting.depth: Single top-down plane at small scale; edits add depth by overlaying a huge mask face in a corner over the tiny gameplay (close-up layer vs tiny figure).

techniques: one flat signature colour per mask (red rooster, yellow tiger, teal helmet)
mask shape as the whole silhouette identity, readable as a huge flat face on black
aftermath persists: bodies and splats stay in the room as a record of the action
stacking score popups (+400pts) with a contrasting outline over the action
flickering dim/bright title text on a static mask
saturated patterned floors (checkerboard, stripes) instead of modelled shading
music hard-cut from combat to ambience on exit
feel: hot magenta floors + flat colour-keyed masks + persistent aftermath + flicker text = tense, loud, cinematic
for_fred: Leave evidence of Fred's gag in the frame after he exits (a splash, a knocked-over prop) so the empty scene still tells the story, and use a giant flat Fred face popping into a corner over a tiny Fred in the scene as a close-up beat.
